title: Daily Temperatures
description:
Given daily temperatures in chronological order, return an array of equal length. At each index, report how many days must pass before a strictly warmer temperature occurs. If no later day is warmer, report 0 for that index. An empty input produces an empty result.

A later day with the same temperature is not warm enough, and a warm day can resolve the waiting periods of several earlier days. Count the distance in indices, not the temperature difference. The answer refers only to later entries; a warmer day that occurred earlier does not count.

The interesting efficiency gain comes from remembering unresolved days in a monotone stack. When a new warm day arrives, it can settle every colder day at the top; the indices still in the stack have not yet seen a strictly warmer value. This avoids comparing every pair of days.

Example 1:

Input: temperatures = [73,74,75,71,69,72,76,73]
Output: [1,1,4,2,1,1,0,0]

Example 2:

Input: temperatures = [30,20,10]
Output: [0,0,0]

Example 3:

Input: temperatures = [30,40]
Output: [1,0]

Constraints:

  • 0 <= temperatures.length <= 100,000.
  • -100 <= temperatures[i] <= 150.
  • Return exactly one nonnegative count per input day.
